The xDev identity

One X.
More things to build.

xDev is where Duy builds products, explores ideas, and shares the practice of making software. One shared signature connects these activities: the blue X.

xDev

Keep the signature.
Extend the expression.

The blue X is the consistent point of recognition. Lighter lettering, gently rounded joins, and open spacing balance the mark. Each product has its own name within the same visual structure.

One family of identities.

DEV is the master identity. AI Studio uses a two-line AI / STUDIO name aligned within the height of the X.

Lighter lettering.
A clear structure.

DEV and AI use uppercase letters with an even stroke and gently rounded joins. The smaller STUDIO line sits beneath AI, within the height of the X. In written content, the brand name remains xDev.

Blue is the signature.

The gradient stays inside the X. Neutral lettering and backgrounds keep the logo clear and legible.

  • X / light blue#7BD4FF
  • X / mid blue#1E90FF
  • X / deep blue#004CFF
  • Type / light background#344568
  • Type / dark background#E8ECF8
  • Dark background#142745

Consistency in every use.

  • Preserve the X

    Use the original symbol, proportions, and gradient.

  • Choose the right background

    Use the light version on light backgrounds and the dark version on dark backgrounds. Avoid visually busy imagery behind the mark.

  • Give it breathing room

    Leave clear space of at least one quarter of the X height around the logo.

  • Preserve proportions

    Do not stretch, rotate, outline, add shadows, or independently recolor the lettering.

  • Check the actual size

    DEV and STUDIO must remain readable on the intended device. Use the standalone X when space is too small.

  • Extend the system

    Add product names using the same letter construction and alignment without altering the X.

Extension study / NOTES

Room for the next idea.

NOTES explores how the identity could extend to writing and the blog. It shares the X and the same lettering rules. This is an extension study, not a newly launched product.
